hazard-classes-addressed.class-id: 1. the Codex child inherits pull-request credentials (GitHub tokens) or other secrets it should not have
hazard-classes-addressed.probed: Ran the two named dispatch tests with GH_TOKEN and an undeclared OPENAI_API_KEY set in the kernel's environment. Then mutated the guard in two stages and ran the named test each time: (a) src/review.ts:360 `if (CREDENTIAL_STORE_REDIRECTIONS.some(...))` -> `if (false && ...)`, disabling the fix-round refusal; (b) additionally `for (const [name, target] of redirected)` -> `redirected.slice(0, 0)` in applyHarnessEnvironment, disabling the second layer, which is the DANGEROUS state rather than the absent feature. Read src/review.ts:586 against :603 to establish the install-then-join ordering, and read the real capture for the in-sandbox key probe.
hazard-classes-addressed.finding:
CR-M6P7B-03. The class itself is bounded, with a two-layer guard and real captured evidence; the finding is that the second guard's composition rests on an untested call order. Stage (a) went RED on the missing refusal while the test's SAFETY assertion still PASSED, because layer 2 held. Stage (b) went RED on the safety assertion itself: `the reviewer was handed HOME /tmp/tiphys-codex-review-raj7hs/kernel-home (the kernel's real HOME is /tmp/tiphys-codex-review-raj7hs/kernel-home) and HOME/.git-credentials reads "https://x:SECRET-TOKEN@github.com
"`, actual `{reviewerHomeGitCredentials: 'https://x:SECRET-TOKEN@github.com
', reviewerHomeIsKernelHome: true}`. Both edits restored; `git status --porcelain` shows only this untracked verdict. Unmutated, test/codex-review.test.ts:282-283 assert GH_TOKEN and OPENAI_API_KEY are ABSENT from the reviewer's environment while the declared CODEX_API_KEY is present, and declaring GH_TOKEN refuses the dispatch with no record and no `out` directory. src/review.ts:586 installs dependencies with childEnv.env BEFORE :603 joins the harness variables, so no install script of the reviewed head sees the key. Sub-command exclusion is real captured output, not a claim: codex-luna.stream.jsonl item_3 runs `/bin/bash -lc "node -e "console.log(process.env.CODEX_API_KEY === undefined ? 'key absent' : 'key present')""` with aggregated_output `key absent
`, exit_code 0.

hazard-classes-addressed.class-id: 2. Codex's sandbox is wider than the grant: network on, or writes outside the review worktree; where Codex has no setting to bound something, the code and work history must say so rather than widen the grant
hazard-classes-addressed.probed: Ran the argv test green, then read the committed real `codex exec --help` for each flag the argv uses and for each of the six `-c` keys it uses. Checked that the grant's data drives the settings rather than a constant (the read-only arm and the four throwing arms). Read the adapter's and the work history's statements of what cannot be bounded. Did not re-run the live CLI measurements (no key; the brief forbids it).
hazard-classes-addressed.finding: CR-M6P7B-01. The class is bounded for the measured CLI and the two genuinely unbounded things are DECLARED rather than widened around: adapters/codex/review.ts:99-109 names the command list (the sandbox bounds what a command touches, not which program runs; execpolicy `allow` means outside the sandbox) and reads (whole-filesystem, as for the Claude executor), and delivery/work-history/m6-p7.md:188-191 says the same. `--ignore-rules` reads "Do not load user or project execpolicy `.rules` files" (codex-exec-help.txt:90-91) and `--ignore-user-config` "Do not load `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`" (:87-88), matching the comment. The grant follows its data: writeReviewWorktree false gives `--sandbox read-only` (test:137) and push / networkTools / readRepository false / a non-plain-word command each throw (test:139-142). The bounds were measured offline with `codex sandbox` WITH CONTROLS (work history :178-184: sibling dir, /tmp and $TMPDIR all "Read-only file system" while workspace-write defaults wrote all four; curl and node https failed DNS while network_access=true reached the network), and a planted `.codex/config.toml` with danger-full-access was not loaded (:185-187). The finding is the residual: the keys are version-specific and silently ignored if unrecognised, and the code comment's own list of limits omits that.

hazard-classes-addressed.class-id: 3. the served model read from text the reviewer wrote instead of Codex's own event stream; a capture without a model read as observed
hazard-classes-addressed.probed: Ran the observer test green, verified the three fixtures' sha256 against the declared hashes in their README, then mutated adapters/codex/review.ts:222 `model: null` -> `model: "gpt-6-luna"` (the requested model as a fallback, the exact defect) and ran both the observer test and the dispatch test. Traced by reading whether a family of `unknown` can satisfy any arm of judgeFamilies.
hazard-classes-addressed.cleared-because: The guard reddened, and a SECOND guard in the kernel caught the same mutation independently of the adapter. The observer test went RED at :157 (`+ 'gpt-6-luna' - null`); the dispatch test went RED with a message from the KERNEL, not the adapter: `no served model was observed: the executor observed gpt-6-luna while the top-level rows name [], so no single served model is established`. So `observedModel` cross-checks an executor's claimed model against the rows that executor also reported, and a fabricated one is refused whatever the adapter says. Restored. Unmutated, the observer hardcodes `model: null` and `topLevelModels: []` (adapters/codex/review.ts:221-225) and never reads the reviewer's messages, and the named test proves the premise rather than assuming it: `keysIn` (test:89-97) walks EVERY key at EVERY depth of the real capture and :154 asserts no row names a model. Fixture hashes I recomputed and matched: codex-luna.stream.jsonl f3bfa353a8e8032add5df4bb40288b8b15b3971b964e5d7b74baa3780f34af9d, codex-without-key.stream.jsonl ee260f4def172e842a1dfa8d16ba168e0f51a6671aff0a269fa96ed9b712a701, codex-exec-help.txt 0e82cfde0122715250e93dc65866caa956b2ac5b9d0b20ec4ad4f9e81486509e. A Codex review therefore always records family `unknown`, and `unknown` satisfies neither the two-distinct-families arm (it is filtered out of `known`) nor the single-family exception (`off` is non-empty for any declared token), so such a review can never form a pair. That is the honest handling of the known limit, carried through to the merge gate rather than stopped at the record.

hazard-classes-addressed.class-id: 4. a family token no one declared compared as if it were a vendor (charter.yaml review-families.available is the list)
hazard-classes-addressed.probed: Ran the families test green, then mutated src/review.ts:986 `families.filter((family) => !listed.includes(family))` -> `... => false && !listed.includes(family)`, so cross-vocabulary tokens are always treated as comparable, and re-ran. Then traced by hand the two configurations this phase actually produces against the committed charter.yaml.
hazard-classes-addressed.cleared-because: The guard reddened on the mutation: `AssertionError: the counted reviews were observed on 2 distinct families (review-a anthropic, review-b openai), from the kernel's records / true !== false` at test:186 - the mutated guard called an undeclared `openai` a distinct vendor, which is the hazard exactly. Restored. The M6-P5 refusal is kept for undeclared tokens and the new green path is narrow: charter.yaml:186 declares `available: [anthropic]`, so a Claude review (`anthropic`) plus a Codex review (`unknown`) gives outside=[unknown] and is RED naming it, and two Codex reviews give known=[] and are RED on the single-family exception. The witness spec witness/m6-p7-families-from-two-vocabularies.json carries two structurally different mutations, not one member of a class.

hazard-classes-addressed.class-id: 5. the default executor moved to charter.yaml review-executor: a missing or wrong value falls back silently, or src/ still names a harness package
hazard-classes-addressed.probed: Grepped the whole tree (excluding node_modules and dist/) for DEFAULT_REVIEW_EXECUTOR to establish that no fallback target survives; read all four refusal routes in configuredReviewExecutor and the caller in src/commands/review.ts; ran the named test's absent-charter arm; ran the existing p7-no-vendor-in-src test; ran `node bin/tiphys.ts validate --type charter charter.yaml`.
hazard-classes-addressed.finding: CR-M6P7B-02. There is no fallback at all - every route is fail-closed - so the class is bounded; the finding is that only one of the four routes is executed by a test. The grep returns only three prose lines in delivery/work-history/m6-p5.md and m6-p7.md: the constant is gone from code. src/commands/review.ts:92-99 refuses with `no --executor was given and <reason>`; configuredReviewExecutor (src/review.ts:70-90) refuses a non-file, an unreadable file, an undecodable document, and a missing / non-string / blank field, each naming the path. p7-no-vendor-in-src: `node --test test/schemas.test.ts test/model-resolution.test.ts` gave 31 tests, 31 pass, 0 fail, including `no vendor model name appears in the kernel's shipped source, schemas, roles or configuration`. The one remaining `@tiphys/claude-code-plugin` under src/ is src/commands/init.ts:33, a doc comment citing DR-0008's published package names, present before this change and not a review-executor default. `validate --type charter charter.yaml` printed nothing (exit 0) with the new optional field.

criteria.quote: p7-build: `npm run build` exits 0, `npm test` exits 0 with 0 fail.
evidence: First half MET: `npm run build` exit 0 on node v26.6.0 in this worktree, including the new `adapters/codex/tsconfig.json` project added to the tsc -b list in package.json.

Second half NOT MET IN THIS CONTAINER, and I am reporting the red rather than rounding it down. `node --test "test/**/*.test.ts"` (what `npm test` runs) on node v26.6.0 with dist/ built: 1246 tests, 1244 pass, 2 fail, 0 skipped, exit 1.

Both failures are in test/license-gate.test.ts (release packaging), a file this change does not touch, and both are one environment cause: `npm install failed: npm error code SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN ... request to https://registry.npmjs.org/ajv failed, reason: self-signed certificate in certificate chain` (:939) and `release-verify: step install exited 1 ... 5 failing step(s)` (:1188). Each took ~284 s, i.e. it spent its time on the network.

I measured the cause directly rather than inferring it from the file name: `node -e 'https.get("https://registry.npmjs.org/ajv")'` in this container prints `ERROR SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN self-signed certificate in certificate chain`. This container's TLS chain is intercepted, and these tests' children run in the scrubbed environment with no TLS setting by design, so they cannot reach the public registry here.

So the two reds are this reviewer's container, not the branch. I did NOT establish the base's result on the same interpreter (CLAUDE.md standing warning 12 asks for that before blaming a change); the direct TLS measurement above is what I have instead, and it explains both failures without reference to the diff. The criterion is finally established by the `suite` gate in CI, and this verdict does not claim it.

deviations-judged.deviation: The plan's acceptance criterion p7-observe requires that "the observer returns the served model from the committed real capture". It does not, and cannot: Codex 0.159.2 names no served model on any event it writes, so the first half of the criterion is not met.
deviations-judged.reasoning: Declared, not concealed, and the consequence is carried through rather than papered over. delivery/work-history/m6-p7.md:221-222 says it in those words: "p7-observe's first half ... is NOT MET with Codex 0.159.2; the second half holds." The premise is a measured property of a committed real capture rather than an assertion - test/codex-review.test.ts:154 walks every key at every depth and asserts none is a model - and the reason string states the mechanism (the binary reads the served model from the API's openai-model response header and prints none of it). Nothing substitutes for the missing observation: the requested model is not a fallback in the adapter, and I confirmed by mutation that the kernel refuses a fabricated one anyway. The effect reaches the merge gate: the record's family is `unknown` and no arm of judgeFamilies can count such a review toward a pair, so the phase cannot silently buy a cheaper pair with an unobserved family. The plan's intent for M6-P7 is that a Codex harness can EXECUTE a review under the grant (DR-0065), which it can; the unmet half is a property of the vendor's CLI, not of this change, and it is the limit the brief records as already reported to the owner.

findings.analysis: The six `-c` keys carry the whole grant (no network, review directory only, no approvals, no web search, the credential excluded from sub-commands), they are version-specific, an unrecognised one is silently ignored rather than an error, and the adapter's own "WHAT THIS CLI CANNOT BOUND, stated rather than widened around" block omits this - which is the one of its limits that degrades with no signal at all.
evidence: delivery/work-history/m6-p7.md:168-170 records the mechanism in the implementer's own words: "`-c` keys, each checked against the installed CLI rather than memory, by giving it a wrong value and reading its own error (unknown keys are silently accepted, exit 0, so a key is only proved by a type error)".

Consequence: with any `codex` on PATH whose config keys differ from 0.159.2's, `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=false` and the two /tmp exclusions are accepted and ignored, and the grant's "no network, review directory only" is not in force.

Nothing in the change can notice. The named test's help check is `argv.filter((part) => /^-/.test(part))` (test/codex-review.test.ts:131), which matches the dash-flags and the literal `-c` but never the key strings, so the six keys are checked against nothing.

The committed help cannot serve as the oracle either. I grepped test/fixtures/review-dispatch/codex-exec-help.txt for all six keys: exactly ONE hit, `shell_environment_policy.inherit` at :25, and that only inside the `-c` usage EXAMPLE. `approval_policy`, `web_search`, `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access`, `.exclude_slash_tmp` and `.exclude_tmpdir_env_var` appear nowhere in it.
adapters/codex/review.ts:11-13 does declare the mapping measured against @openai/codex 0.159.2, but the limits block at :99-109 names only the command list and reads.

Why this is low and not blocking: on the measured CLI the bounds were verified with real controls (work history :178-184), the adapter names its version, no defect is reachable with 0.159.2 on PATH, and the `codex` CLI is not a dependency of this repository, so its version is purely environmental.
findings.concrete-fix: Two parts, both small. (1) Add a fourth bullet to the WHAT THIS CLI CANNOT BOUND block in adapters/codex/review.ts: this CLI accepts an unrecognised `-c` key silently and exits 0, so every key here is proved only against 0.159.2 and a different version can ignore one with no signal. (2) Give it a signal. Cheapest: have `sandboxArgs` also emit `--strict-config`, after MEASURING (the same way the keys were measured) whether 0.159.2 errors on an unknown `-c` key with it set - its help at codex-exec-help.txt:33-35 promises only "Error out when config.toml contains fields that are not recognized by this version of Codex", so whether that covers `-c` overrides is a measurement, not an assumption, and if it does not, say so in the comment. Failing that, have the adapter run `codex --version` once and refuse to build an argv for a version it was not measured against, which turns a silent widening into a refused dispatch.

findings.analysis: Of the four ways `review-executor` can be missing or wrong, only one is executed by a test, and the untested arm is the one every existing project in the fleet will hit first.
evidence: configuredReviewExecutor (src/review.ts:70-90) has four distinct refusal routes: not a regular file, unreadable, undecodable, and `names no review-executor` (a missing, non-string or blank field).
The named test exercises only the first: test/codex-review.test.ts:411-413 builds a project with NO charter.yaml at all and asserts `/no --executor was given and .*charter\.yaml could not be read/`.

The arm a real project hits - a charter.yaml that exists and validates but predates this field, which is every charter in the fleet until it is edited - has no test, and its message (`names no review-executor`) is the one an operator would actually read.

I confirmed the code path is fail-closed by reading it and by grepping the tree for a surviving DEFAULT_REVIEW_EXECUTOR (none in code), so this is a coverage gap on a correct guard, not a defect. An edit that collapsed the four routes back into a fallback would be caught only for the absent-file case.
findings.concrete-fix: Extend the existing named test with a third project built by `project("kind: charter\n")` - a charter that exists and names no review-executor - and assert exit 1, no record, and `/no --executor was given and .*names no review-executor/`. Two lines, the same helper already in the file, and it pins the message the operator sees.

findings.analysis: The fix round's new guard cannot see the documented bare-string extension form, and the composition is safe only because of an untested call order. No reachable defect today; a guard for a HIGH finding resting on an unstated ordering is worth one line.
evidence: `refuseCredentialStorePointer` (src/review.ts:359-370) reads `entry.name`, but `ChildEnvExtensionEntry` documents a bare-string form (src/exec/env.ts, `extensionName`), and `checkReviewExecutor` (src/review.ts:245-247) validates `environment` with nothing but `Array.isArray`, so a plugin can hand the kernel `environment: ["HOME"]`.

Probe EXECUTED in this worktree against the real modules: `refuseExtraAllowlist(["HOME"], "reason-required")` -> refused ("the allowlist extension entry HOME carries no reason field at all"); `refuseCredentialStorePointer(["HOME"])` -> ACCEPTED.
For `[{name:"HOME",reason:"r"}]` the first ACCEPTS and the second refuses, so the two guards have complementary blind spots on exactly each other's shapes.

Safe only because src/review.ts:541 (refuseExtraAllowlist, reason-required) runs before :546 (refuseCredentialStorePointer) and a bare string can never carry a reason. I could not construct an entry that both guards accept, so nothing is reachable today; nothing states or tests the ordering the safety depends on.
findings.concrete-fix: One line: in refuseCredentialStorePointer compare `extensionName(entry)` (already exported from src/exec/env.ts, the module this one already imports the redirections from) instead of `entry.name`, and widen the parameter type to `readonly ChildEnvExtensionEntry[]` so both guards accept the same shapes. Then add `["HOME"]` as a third arm of the existing pointer test, which reddens today against the current spelling.
